newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Maskhadov set to win Chechen vote outright.
newsitem.headline: Maskhadov set to win Chechen vote outright.

text.p: Aslan Maskhadov, who led Chechnya's tiny guerrilla army to victory over Russian forces last year, is likely to be elected president with more than 50 percent of Monday's vote, a electoral official said on Tuesday.

"There's a very great likelihood he'll go through on the first round," Bilal Ozdemirov of the Central Electoral Commission told reporters. Hardline guerrilla leader Shamil Basayev was second. Ten to 20 percent of votes were counted. Maskhadov needed 50 percent to avoid a second-round run-off.

Ozdemirov said turnout at 9 p.m. (1800 GMT) on Monday, an hour before polls closed, was estimated at 61 percent or 265,000 votes. The closing time was extended by two hours to cope with long queues and he said many polling stations had wanted even more time to clear them.
Speaking outside the Commission headquarters in devastated central Grozny, Commission member Ozdemirov said Maskhadov led in virtually every polling station across the region which had returned data.
Maskhadov's margin over Basayev was generally greater than that between Basayev and the third-placed candidate, acting president Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev, Ozdemirov said.
A preliminary result could be available "towards lunchtime", he added. That would suggest a time very approximately around 1100 GMT.
